title: Microburst sensitivity and stable throughput benchmark for TP/PP distributed inference
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a repeatable benchmark and load-testing harness to measure multi-GPU distributed inference throughput and latency tail behavior under microburst and steady-state traffic for tensor-parallel (TP), pipeline-parallel (PP), and hybrid topologies. The harness will produce tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency series, quantile drift detection, and automated regression alerts for nightly CI runs. Scope includes synthetic and replayed real-trace workloads, configurable KV-cache warm/cold regimes, batching policies, sequence length distributions, and node failure/fallback scenarios.
motivation: Existing throughput tests focus on sustained concurrency across many GPUs but miss short-duration microbursts and sensitivity to pipeline bubble behavior. Customer-facing outages and increased p95 regression alerts have shown that microburst behavior and cross-rank synchronization latencies can cause transient SLO violations. We need a focused harness to reproduce, quantify, and prevent regressions tied to kernel changes, batching logic, and routing policies.
success_metrics: Deterministic tokens/sec baseline for each topology and model size (±5% variance) across 5 runs
p95 and p99 latency time-series exported to Influx/Grafana for every run
Microburst-response matrix: percent SLO breaches when injecting bursts of 10x, 50x, and 100x baseline QPS for 50ms, 200ms, 1s
Automated regression detector with <5% false positive rate over 30 days of historical data
CI job that runs nightly and fails the PR when regression detector flags a confirmed drop in tokens/sec or rise in p95
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness can run TP, PP, and hybrid topologies on multi-node clusters with a single config file
Workloads include synthetic (Zipf and uniform prompt length distributions) and replayed production traces (anonymized), selectable via CLI
Exported metrics: tokens/sec, in-flight requests, p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel utilization, GPU memory peaks, and KV cache hit rate
Microburst injection mode that schedules short-duration high-QPS spikes and records recovery time to baseline
Regression detection pipeline implemented (EWMA + quantile change detector) with a documented alert threshold and dashboard
Documentation and runbook added: how to run locally, in CI, and interpret results; include example Grafana dashboards and run artifacts links
test_cases: Sustained throughput: 60s ramp to target QPS, measure steady-state tokens/sec and latencies
Microburst short spike: inject 100ms 10x spike and record recovery time and p95
Microburst long spike: inject 1s 50x spike to observe pipeline bubble propagation
KV-cache cold start: empty caches before run, measure first-token latency and subsequent improvement
Mixed sequences: 2/4/8k token prompts mixture to validate kernel scheduling and quantization paths
Node failure graceful degradation: kill one worker mid-run and ensure fallback models maintain throughput if configured
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Initial scoping doc written; validated with runtime and infra teams. Decided to support A100 and H100 variants for parity testing.
2026-02-24: Prototype harness implemented in Python using asyncio + grpc load generator. Basic TP-only runs showing reproducible tokens/sec baseline across 3 runs.
2026-03-02: Added microburst injection scheduler and started capturing latency time-series to Influx. Observed 30-40% p95 spikes for PP topologies on 4-stage pipelines during 200ms bursts.
2026-03-08: Implemented EWMA-based regression detector and smoke-tested on 14 days of historical run data. Tuned alpha and threshold to reduce false positives.
2026-03-10: PR opened with harness core and test configs. CI job skeleton added to nightly pipeline (runtime-nightly/bench). Seeking design review from infra and observations team.
notes: Prefer using the same gRPC request shapes as production API to capture realistic serialization and tokenization overheads.
Consider adding a 'cold-network' mode to simulate VPC-on-prem network variance (packet delay/ jitter) as part of failure scenarios.
We should annotate runs with kernel versions and operator flags to correlate regressions with upstream runtime changes.
Keep the replay traces anonymized and limited to sequence length distribution rather than actual prompt content for privacy.
Follow-up task: add multi-tenant interference tests to measure how best-effort background workloads affect priority requests.
owner_notes: Assignee will coordinate with infra to reserve test clusters for nightly runs. Use ephemeral namespaces to avoid collisions.
Budget: estimate ~120 GPU-hours/month for nightly matrix across topologies; coordinate with finance for chargeback.
Plan to open a public-facing benchmark page summarizing stable baselines after initial validation
